title: Ultimate Speed/Feed Orchestrator — Full System Integration
description: Build SpeedFeedOrchestratorEngine that wires ALL existing PRISM assets into a single unified speed/feed pipeline. Every physical input (machine, spindle, holder, tool, material, workholding, coolant, geometry, CAM software, toolpath strategy) is resolved from catalogs and fed through physics models with full stochastic uncertainty. User can provide ANY subset of inputs — engine infers the rest with appropriate confidence degradation.

units.title: SpeedFeedOrchestratorEngine — Core Resolver Architecture
units.description: Create SpeedFeedOrchestratorEngine with the input resolver pipeline. Accept high-level inputs (machine_name, tool_id, material, operation, geometry), resolve each via existing engines/catalogs to full physical specs, then delegate to UltimateSpeedFeedEngine. Key: every unresolved input inflates uncertainty proportionally.
acceptance_criteria: Engine accepts OrchestratorInput with 60+ optional fields across 10 categories
Machine resolver: name/model → machine-profiles-catalog → power, torque, RPM, rigidity
Tool resolver: catalog_id → ToolCatalogEngine → geometry, grade, coating, stickout
Material resolver: name → MaterialRegistry → ISO group, HB, σ_y, k, machinability
Holder resolver: holder_id → holder catalogs → taper, TIR, stiffness, max RPM
Workholding resolver: type → WorkholdingIntelligenceEngine → clamp force, part rigidity
Coolant resolver: type+pressure → CoolantDynamicsEngine → h, effectiveness
Geometry resolver: thin_wall/pocket_depth/overhang → rigidity derating factors
Confidence tracking: each resolved vs inferred vs defaulted field gets confidence score
Delegates to UltimateSpeedFeedEngine with fully resolved params
Returns AtomicValue<OrchestratorResult> with S/F + limiting_factor_chain + confidence

units.title: Machine Resolution Layer — Full Kinematic Integration
units.description: Wire machine-profiles-catalog (910 machines), machine-kinematics-catalog (250 kinematic chains), and MachineMatcherEngine into the orchestrator. Resolve: spindle taper → holder compatibility, guideway type → damping ratio, axis speeds → feed rate limits, controller → look-ahead/block-rate, machine age → degradation factor.
acceptance_criteria: Fuzzy match machine name to catalog via MachineMatcherEngine
Extract: power_kW, max_rpm, torque_Nm, taper, guideway, controller from profile
Kinematic chain: resolve stiffness at tool tip from spindle→holder→tool chain
Guideway type mapping: box_way→ζ=0.05, linear_guide→ζ=0.02, hydrostatic→ζ=0.08
Controller: Fanuc→64-block lookahead, Siemens→128, Heidenhain→256 → max contour feed
Age factor: if machine_hours provided, degrade stiffness by (1 - hours/200000 * 0.3)
If machine not found: use generic profile with confidence=0.4

units.title: Tool + Holder Resolution Layer — Full Tooling System
units.description: Wire ToolCatalogEngine (46K tools), holder catalogs (1164 holders), InsertGradeSelectionEngine (50 grades), CollisionDetectionEngine into the orchestrator. Resolve: solid vs insert body, insert grade → speed factor, holder type → TIR + stiffness, collet/sleeve → additional TIR, tool assembly stiffness from cantilever beam model.
acceptance_criteria: Tool catalog lookup by ID, or by specs (diameter, flutes, material, coating)
Insert grade resolution: grade → material speed multiplier from InsertGradeSelectionEngine
Holder type effects: shrink_fit→TIR=0.003mm, hydraulic→0.003, ER_collet→0.010, Weldon→0.015
Holder stiffness from catalog: BIG DAISHOWA, Haimer, Guhring data
Tool assembly stiffness: k_tool = 3EI/L³ with composite holder+tool+insert
Collet/sleeve: if ER collet, add 0.005mm TIR, reduce stiffness by 15%
Collision check: verify tool assembly fits in machine envelope
If tool not found: infer from diameter/flutes/material with confidence=0.5

units.title: Material + Workholding + Coolant Resolution Layer
units.description: Wire MaterialRegistry (2957 materials), WorkholdingIntelligenceEngine, FixtureClampingEngine, CoolantDynamicsEngine. Resolve material to full physical properties with scatter, workholding to part rigidity and max safe cutting force, coolant to effective heat transfer coefficient.
acceptance_criteria: Material: name → MaterialRegistry → ISO group, HB, σ_y, UTS, k, ρ, Cp, machinability_index
Material scatter: kc1.1 CV=8-12%, mc CV=5-8% from StochasticCuttingForceEngine DB
Workholding: type (vise/chuck/fixture/vacuum/magnetic) → clamp force, part stiffness
Part rigidity: thin_wall_mm, overhang_mm, unsupported_length → derating on ap/ae
Max safe force: from clamp force and friction → upper bound on Fc
Coolant: type+pressure+concentration → CoolantDynamicsEngine → h (W/m²K), effectiveness
Coolant speed factor: flood→1.0, mist→0.85, MQL→0.80, dry→0.70, cryo→1.15
If material not found: fuzzy match + confidence=0.5, warn user

units.title: Stochastic Integration Layer — Full Uncertainty Pipeline
units.description: Wire StochasticCuttingForceEngine, StochasticToolLifeEngine, StochasticChatterEngine, StochasticSurfaceFinishEngine, UncertaintyPropagationPipelineEngine into the orchestrator. Every S/F output gets CI95, Sobol sensitivity, P(chatter), reliability curve.
acceptance_criteria: Force uncertainty: StochasticCuttingForceEngine with material scatter → Fc CI95
Tool life uncertainty: StochasticToolLifeEngine → Weibull life distribution, P(survive)
Chatter risk: StochasticChatterEngine → P(chatter) at recommended speed/depth
Surface finish uncertainty: StochasticSurfaceFinishEngine → Ra CI95, Cpk
Cross-engine propagation: UncertaintyPropagationPipelineEngine chains Force→Life→Finish
Confidence inflation for unknowns: each defaulted input widens CI by its importance weight
Overall confidence score: product of all resolver confidences × stochastic confidence
Sobol sensitivity: which input uncertainty dominates output uncertainty
Output includes: dominant_uncertainty_source, suggested_measurement for improvement

units.title: Playbook + Stability + Safety Integration
units.description: Wire MachiningPlaybookEngine (296 rules), ChatterStabilityLobeEngine, GCodeSafetyAnalyzerEngine into the orchestrator. Apply domain expert rules, check stability lobes, validate safety limits.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook query: operation+material+conditions → applicable rules/warnings/tips
Rules that modify S/F: e.g., 'reduce feed 30% for interrupted cut in titanium'
Stability lobe check: if stiffness+natural_freq known, check if speed/depth in stable zone
If in chatter zone: suggest alternative RPM from nearest stable pocket
Power check: P_cutting < machine_power × 0.8 (safety margin)
Torque check: T_cutting < max_torque × 0.8
Deflection check: δ < tolerance/3 (δ from cantilever beam model)
Feed rate limit: Vf < machine max_feed_rate
Output: safety_checks[], playbook_warnings[], stability_assessment

units.title: Dispatcher Wiring + calcDispatcher Actions
units.description: Wire SpeedFeedOrchestratorEngine to calcDispatcher with comprehensive actions. Add exports to index.ts. Create orchestrator-specific action schemas.
acceptance_criteria: Actions: sf_orchestrate (full pipeline), sf_resolve_machine, sf_resolve_tool, sf_resolve_material
Actions: sf_stochastic (full UQ mode), sf_quick (fast mode skipping stochastic)
Actions: sf_compare (compare 2+ scenarios), sf_optimize (multi-objective Pareto)
Compact formatter for each action
All wired to calcDispatcher ACTIONS array and switch cases
Exports added to engines/index.ts

units.title: CAM Software + Toolpath Strategy Resolution Layer
units.description: Wire CAM strategy databases (433 strategies across 20 CAM systems), CrossCamRecommenderEngine, NovelToolpathEngine, EngagementAdaptiveFeedEngine, InstantaneousEngagementEngine, MotionDynamicsProfileEngine, ToolpathSmoothingEngine, and TribalKnowledgeEngine into the orchestrator. User specifies CAM software + strategy name, orchestrator resolves effective engagement, chip thinning model, feed adaptation mode, and pulls strategy-specific tribal knowledge.
acceptance_criteria: Accept cam_software (Mastercam/hyperMILL/Fusion360/NX/SolidCAM/etc) + strategy_name
Resolve strategy to effective ae/ap from MultiCamStrategy DB (256 strategies, 13 CAMs)
Toolpath type classification: conventional/adaptive/trochoidal/HSM/HPC/plunge/constant-chip-load
Chip thinning correction: if ae < 50% Dc, apply fz_eff = fz * Dc/(2*sqrt(ae*(Dc-ae)))
Adaptive/trochoidal mode: boost Vc by 1.5-3x, reduce ae to 5-15% Dc, keep chip load constant
Motion dynamics: MotionDynamicsProfileEngine corner decel + controller look-ahead limits
Actual vs programmed feed: ToolpathSmoothingEngine Frenet-Serret curvature feed reduction
Variable engagement: InstantaneousEngagementEngine for pocket corners, entry arcs
Novel toolpath physics: if TGAR/HRAF/CFSF strategy, use NovelToolpathEngine force models
Tribal knowledge: pull CAM-specific tips from 2800+ tips DB for strategy+material combo
If CAM not specified: use generic strategy classification with confidence=0.6
Output: effective_ae_mm, effective_ap_mm, feed_mode, speed_multiplier, strategy_warnings[]

units.title: User Tool Library + Persistent Tool Crib
units.description: Create a persistent user tool library system where users can add, remove, and organize their actual owned tools. Can import from catalog by ID, manually enter custom tools, or bulk import CSV. Each tool stores: catalog_id (if from PRISM catalog), geometry (diameter, flutes, flute_length, OAL, corner_radius), material/coating, holder_type, typical stickout, notes, purchase_date, current_condition. Library persists in localStorage with optional cloud sync. The orchestrator uses this library instead of the full 46K catalog when user has tools saved.
acceptance_criteria: UserToolLibrary data model: id, catalog_ref?, geometry, material, coating, holder, stickout, condition, notes
CRUD operations: add from catalog search, add manual, edit, remove, duplicate
Bulk import: CSV with columns matching tool fields
Tool condition tracking: new/good/worn/needs_regrind/retired
Holder pairing: each tool can have a default holder from holder catalog
Storage: localStorage with JSON export/import for backup
Integration with orchestrator: if user has tool library, filter S/F candidates to owned tools only
Fallback: if no owned tools qualify for a feature, suggest catalog tools to purchase
Tool magazine mapping: user can assign tools to magazine positions per machine

units.title: Part Geometry Analysis + Feature-to-Toolpath Recommendation
units.description: Build a pipeline that accepts uploaded CAD (STEP/STL) or print (PDF with dimensions) and extracts machinable features, then matches features to user's tool library and recommends optimal toolpath strategy + S/F for each operation. Uses FeatureRecognitionEngine for geometry, CollisionDetectionEngine for tool fit, CrossCamRecommenderEngine for strategy ranking, OperationSequencerEngine for order, and ToolMagazineOptimizationEngine for tool change minimization.
acceptance_criteria: Accept STEP, STL, or PDF upload in web UI
Feature extraction: pockets (open/closed), holes (through/blind), walls (thin/thick), contours, faces, slots, threads
Per feature: extract depth_mm, width_mm, corner_radius_mm, surface_finish_req, tolerance_mm
Tool qualification filter: from user library, find tools where diameter fits, flute_length >= depth, no collision
CollisionDetectionEngine: verify tool+holder clears part geometry at required depth
Strategy recommendation per feature: CrossCamRecommenderEngine ranks strategies filtered by user's CAM software
Multi-tool optimization: rough with large tool, semi-finish with medium, finish with small
RestMachiningEngine: compute remaining stock after each operation for next tool
OperationSequencerEngine: order operations for minimum setup changes
ToolMagazineOptimizationEngine: minimize tool changes, suggest magazine layout
Full job output: ordered operation list with tool, strategy, S/F, estimated time per op
DfMRulesEngine: flag features that are unmachrinable or need special attention
If no user tools qualify: suggest specific catalog tools to purchase with links
PDF print analysis: OCR dimensions and tolerances from 2D drawings (best-effort)

units.title: Web UI - Speed/Feed Calculator Page + User Preferences
units.description: Build a dedicated SpeedFeedPage in the web app that calls SpeedFeedOrchestratorEngine via MCP. Includes: persistent user preferences (default CAM software, default machine, default material), CAM software quick-switcher in the S/F page header, toolpath strategy dropdown filtered by selected CAM, and full input form with smart defaults from user prefs. All results show confidence bands and limiting factor chain.
acceptance_criteria: New route /speed-feed in web app (separate from existing /calculator)
User preferences stored in localStorage: default_cam, default_machine, default_material, default_holder_type, default_coolant
Settings gear icon on S/F page opens inline preferences panel (not buried in separate settings page)
CAM software selector: dropdown of 20 supported CAMs with icons, persists as default
Quick-switch CAM: pill/chip bar at top of page showing current CAM, click to change instantly
Toolpath strategy dropdown: filtered by selected CAM software, shows only strategies available in that CAM
Strategy descriptions: hover tooltip explains each strategy (e.g. 'Dynamic Milling: constant chip load, 5-15% ae')

Input sections: Material (searchable dropdown from 2957 materials), Tool (diameter/flutes/coating or catalog search), Machine (searchable from 910 profiles or manual entry), Workholding (type selector), Coolant (type+pressure)
Smart defaults: when user selects machine from catalog, auto-fill power/rpm/torque/taper
Results panel: S/F values with confidence bars, limiting factor highlighted in red/yellow/green
Uncertainty toggle: switch between 'Quick' (no stochastic) and 'Full Analysis' (CI95, Sobol)
Playbook warnings panel: shows applicable machining rules/tips for current setup
Export: copy S/F as text, or download as setup sheet PDF

units.title: Tests — Exhaustive Validation + Integration
units.description: Comprehensive test suite covering: resolver accuracy, catalog lookups, stochastic propagation, playbook integration, edge cases (unknown machine, unknown material, minimal input).
acceptance_criteria: Machine resolution: known machine → correct specs
Tool resolution: catalog ID → correct geometry
Material resolution: name → correct ISO group and properties
Minimal input test: just material+diameter → valid S/F with low confidence
Full input test: all 60+ fields → high confidence S/F
Stochastic output: CI95 brackets mean for force, life, Ra
Chatter check: known unstable point returns P(chatter) > 0.5
Playbook integration: titanium milling returns relevant warnings
Safety checks: over-power scenario returns power_exceeded
Confidence degradation: more unknowns → wider CI, lower confidence
All 30+ tests passing
